mechanism_narrative: The consistent four-week trend of improving RETAIL_REC mobility, moving from -32.3% to -21.9%, indicates a sustained recovery in consumer activity that will continue to drive retail and recreation visits higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the average of the last 28 days, or the improving trend reverses for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: As WORKPLACES mobility continues its strong recovery, approaching pre-baseline levels, it signals a critical mass of people returning to offices and urban centers, which will directly translate into increased foot traffic for retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: WORKPLACES mobility fails to rise above -10% within the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC declines despite WORKPLACES reaching this threshold.

mechanism_narrative: The concurrent and sustained improvement in both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility indicates a broad-based return to daily commuting and out-of-home routines. This synchronized behavioral shift will drive increased discretionary activity, boosting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: Either TRANSIT or WORKPLACES mobility shows a decline for two consecutive weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not improve despite continued recovery in both.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility and concurrent rise in other categories strongly suggests an ongoing easing of public health restrictions or a lack of new restrictive policies. This stable policy environment enables continued recovery in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: New government restrictions on movement or gatherings are announced, or RESIDENTIAL mobility shows a sustained increase for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The steady decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility, indicating fewer people staying home, will immediately translate into more opportunities for out-of-home activities. This shift will provide an immediate boost to RETAIL_REC over the next week.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL mobility falls below 10% from baseline
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility increases above 11% in the next week, or RETAIL_REC declines despite RESIDENTIAL falling below 10%.

mechanism_narrative: The sustained positive trend in GROCERY_PHARM mobility, indicating stable essential activity, combined with the improving trend in RETAIL_REC, suggests growing consumer confidence and a willingness to engage in discretionary spending, driving further retail recovery over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM mobility drops below its 4-week average (11.5%) or RETAIL_REC shows a decline for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A significant rebound in PARKS mobility, after a period of stagnation, would signal increased public comfort with outdoor leisure activities. This renewed engagement with public spaces is a leading indicator for broader out-of-home activity, including retail and recreation, over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility rises by more than 5 percentage points week-on-week
failure_condition: PARKS mobility does not increase by more than 5 percentage points week-on-week, or RETAIL_REC declines despite such an increase.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent and accelerating shift of people away from residential locations, as evidenced by the steady decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility from 16.4% to 10.6%, reflects a fundamental change in daily routines that will continue to channel activity towards retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility shows an increase for two consecutive weeks, indicating a reversal of the trend towards more time at home.
